title: MONOLITH DISSOLUTION — identifying the snakes
principle: A monolith is perishable. It rots because it grows without structure. Snakes = entangled code that should be separate. Lions = code that SHOULD be monolithic (it's irreducibly one thing). Extract snakes. Keep lions.
what_makes_a_snake: It has a clear name (FLOOD, THYMUS, GLASS)
It has clear inputs and outputs
It only talks to 2-3 globals (ctx, breathT, R)
It could be tested in isolation
Adding to it doesn't break other things
Removing it doesn't break the rest
It was added AFTER the core was working
what_makes_a_lion: It IS the core (project(), resize(), the canvas element)
It can't be tested in isolation — it IS the isolation
Splitting it creates two broken halves, not two working parts
It was there from the beginning

globe.js.why_snake: render() is 735 lines because it's 12 sub-snakes tangled together. Each sub-snake draws one visual layer. They don't need each other.

effects.js.why_snake: Each effect is independent. Removing one doesn't break others. They only share breathT and ctx.

sensors.js.why_snake: Cleanest I/O. Input=fetch, Output=arrays. The render just reads the arrays. Logic and rendering are already separate in concept, just tangled in location.

canvas-view.js.why_snake: Only runs when user switches views. Globe doesn't need it. It doesn't need the globe (except one snapshot moment). Most independent.

lions.project(): The 3D→2D projection. Everything depends on it. It IS the globe. Lion.
lions.resize(): The canvas dimensions. Everything reads W, H, cx, cy, R. Lion.
lions.tick(): The animation frame loop. It IS the heartbeat. Lion.
lions.mulberry32(): The PRNG. Everything seeded from it. Lion. (Already extracted to js/mulberry32.js)
lions.PINS[]: The pin data. Everything renders it. Lion. (Already extracted to js/pins.js)

dissolution_order: 3. effects.js THIRD (8 small effects, 280 lines freed)
4. globe.js LAST (the core, needs everything else gone first)
temporal: Not all at once. Each sow checks. Each sow extracts what's ready. The snakes dissolve one by one. The lions remain.
